question.leadin: This politically-motivated event was perpetrated by activists who exited the Old South Meeting House dressed as Native Americans.
question.text: Name this event in which a group of rebellious colonists dumped over 300 chests of a certain British good into a Massachusetts harbor.
question.clue: The Beaver, Eleanor, and Dartmouth weren't allowed by Governor Thomas Hutchinson to return to England, leading to this event.

swap.leadin: The command "Don't fire until you see the whites of their eyes" was issued during this battle.
swap.text: Name this June 1775 battle in which American forces lost to a British army on the outskirts of Boston. The location of this battle was actually at Breed's Hill, not at its namesake location.
swap.clue: William Prescott constructed a defensive redoubt at this battle, which resulted in the dismissal of Thomas Gage.

question.text: Following the Revolutionary War Battles of Germantown and Brandywine, troops retreated to this Pennsylvania encampment. Washington's army had to suffer through the harsh winter of 1777 in this location.
question.clue: Baron von Steuben taught soldiers at this location proper bayonet training and other European drills.

swap.text: Opposition to the Constitution was led by this Virginian politician who famously claimed "give me liberty or give me death!"
swap.clue: He declined to attend the Constitutional Convention, claiming that he "smelt a rat in Philadelphia".

question.text: The first major American casualty was this Major General of Irish descent, who led the attack of Quebec City with Benedict Arnold.
question.clue: At the second Battle of Quebec, during the Revolutionary War, Benedict Arnold commanded the American troops along with this Irish-born general, who was killed in action.

swap.leadin: According to this person, a certain animal is "a little vain and silly" but "would not hesitate to attack a Grenadier of the British Guards."
swap.text: Name this person who called the same animal "a true original native of America." This man was also the oldest delegate to the Constitutional Convention.
swap.clue: He served on the Committee of Five and indirectly prompted Louis XVI to sign the Edict of Versailles while an ambassador.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of History of the United States.
question.text: A nine-volume History of the United States of America 1801-1817 was written by a member of this family with the first name Henry, who also wrote a posthumously published autobiography about his Education.
question.clue: Letters between a woman with this surname and her husband warn of "the despotism of the petticoat" and the fomenting of a rebellion.

swap.text: This American privateer fought in the American Revolution and famously said "I have not begun to fight!" aboard his command, the Bonhomme Richard.
swap.clue: This naval commander raided English coastal towns during the American Revolution, and defeated the British sloop HMS Drake in 1778.

question.leadin: Name these people from the life of Aaron Burr.
question.text: In 1776, Burr was appointed aide to this general, who said "Don't fire until you see the whites of their eyes" at Bunker Hill.
question.clue: He was second-in-command to Artemas Ward in the Army of Observation, and along with Ward, Philip Schuyler and Charles Lee, was one of four major generals appointed by the Continental Congress in 1775.

swap.text: This loser at Saratoga was known as "Gentleman Johnny" and took Fort Ticonderoga and Fort Edward before losing at Saratoga.
swap.clue: This British general commanded at Saratoga. He was to rejoin William Howe in Albany following the battle, but was abandoned by Howe and had to surrender outright.

question.leadin: Name these following about a race described in Greek myth.
question.text: 1. points) Tarleton was captured during this May-October 1781 siege that ended with the surrender of Cornwallis.
question.clue: An apocryphal story holds that the band of the losing army at a siege in this city played "The World Turn'd Upside Down."

swap.leadin: Identify the following about a Revolutionary War battle.
swap.text: This British commander-in-chief and governor of remarked after the Red Coats' three charges up , "One more victory like that will destroy us."
swap.clue: This British general's wife Margaret may have leaked his plans for a secret night march to capture Samuel Adams and John Hancock at Lexington. William Howe replaced this general after the Battle of Bunker Hill.

question.text: After Leclerc died of yellow fever, he was replaced by a cruel military commander from this family. A French count from this family led the U.S. naval blockade at the Battle of Yorktown.
question.clue: This general's son surrendered to Jacques Dessalines shortly before the declaration of Haitian independence.

swap.leadin: Accused of being a loyalist for voting against the Declaration of Independence, he quickly silenced doubters with his "Declaration...Setting Forth the Causes and Necessities of their Taking Up Arms"
swap.text: Name this "Penman of the Revolution" whose wrote a series of letters defending the Constitution under the name Fabius.
swap.clue: Along with Thomas McKean, he was one of the two members of the Continental Congress to enter the military, and he opposed John Adams in the Continental Congress by voting against the Declaration of Independence.

question.leadin: This man protested the Stamp Act's "chains of slavery" ironically by having his own slaves walk around with protest banners.
question.text: Name this Virginia senator whose namesake resolution at the Second Continental Congress led to the Declaration of Independence a month later. One of his relatives would later eulogize George Washington as "first in war, first in peace, and first in the hearts of his countrymen."
question.answerHtml: Richard Henry Lee [do not accept “Light-Horse” Harry Lee]
question.clue: In 1765, he co-authored the Westmoreland Resolves, which promised "danger and disgrace" to those who paid the taxes enforced by the Stamp Act.

swap.text: This notorious British soldier known as the "Butcher" reportedly reveled in abuse of prisoners at Charleston. His men were accused of massacring Americans at the Battle of Waxhaws.
swap.clue: This man's division, the Green Dragoons, skirmished with American horsemen at the Battle of Guilford Courthouse.

question.leadin: This woman's second husband, Joseph Ashburn, was taken captive by the British, and she went on to marry John Claypoole.
question.text: Identify this woman who was supposedly visited by George Washington in 1776 to create a flag for the new nation.
question.clue: The first flag of the United States was legendarily created by this seamstress.

swap.leadin: This man issued a 1775 proclamation promising freedom for any slave who escaped to join the Loyalist cause, later organizing them into the "Ethiopian Regiment."
swap.text: Name this last royal governor of Virginia, more famous for a namesake war he fought against Native Americans.
swap.clue: This man's forces were defeated at the Battle of Great Bridge, and he set Norfolk on fire with a naval bombardment.

question.leadin: Answer the following about an American frontiersman.
question.text: This man took part in the 1784 settlers' revolt against North Carolina. He was elected as the first governor of the state of Franklin and later served as the first governor of Tennessee.
question.clue: Along with James Robertson, this Virginian founded the Watauga settlement and he would later lead 250 frontiersmen to victory at King's Mountain.

swap.text: Lee also led troops at this last major battle in the Carolinas during the Revolution. Despite winning a tactical victory here over Nathanael Greene, Alexander Stewart was forced to retreat to Charleston until the end of the war.
swap.clue: Often called the bloodiest battle of the Revolution, this September 1781 assault on Alexander Stewart deteriorated into a raid on the British wine supplies, but nonetheless trapped Stewart's forces in Charlestown for the rest of the war.
